images.title: Two fields in 45 plots
images.purpose: Show that 4/5 and 7/9 of two equal fields become 36 and 35 plots out of 45, so 4/5 is greater.
images.composition: Two equal square fields side by side with wide space between them, and one comparison line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Left: one square field divided by thin grey #6B7280 lines into a grid of 5 equal columns and 9 equal rows, 45 equal plots; the left 4 columns, 36 plots, filled teal #0072B2, with thicker lines between columns. Right: one square field of exactly the same size, the same 5 by 9 grid of 45 equal plots; the bottom 7 rows, 35 plots, filled amber #E69F00, with thicker lines between rows. Centred below: one comparison line. Exactly 2 fields, 45 plots each, 36 teal, 35 amber.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: Multiply the denominators to get a common unit, then compare the numerators.
images.description: Two same-size square fields, each a 5 by 9 grid of 45 equal plots: 4 columns shaded teal give 36/45 and 7 rows shaded amber give 35/45, so 4/5 > 7/9 by just 1 plot.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say how the fifths and the ninths both become plots of the same size in each field.

image_decisions.why: A grid of the same 45 plots in both fields shows why multiplying the denominators gives a common unit.
